title: GCSE mocks: 8-week daily revision plan
note: Specification-led, daily retrieval, exam questions, heavier weekends. The mock date is not confirmed: treat Week 8 as the final week before mocks and shift the start if needed. If your school has not taught a section, label it NOT TAUGHT and ask whether the mock assesses it; do not silently skip it. For the OCR Literature modern text, 19th-century novel and poetry cluster use the exact texts your school teaches.
targets: German (6 days/week): 30 new official-list items a day until the list is covered; review 40-60 older items. Test German to English and English to German. On a hard day do 15 new + the full review rather than skip.

English Literature (4-5 days/week): 2-3 quotations a day, each with speaker, situation, method, interpretation and theme/context. About 25 reliable Romeo and Juliet quotations by the end of Week 4, then maintain. Same daily target for the other texts once confirmed.
Science: 10-15 facts/key terms per session and 5 equations where relevant. Every set needs at least one application or practical/data question.
Geography: 8-12 facts/process steps per session; 3-5 precise case-study facts per case-study session (location, causes, effects, responses, evidence).
Economics: 8-12 definitions/relationships per session; two causal chains and one balanced judgement each week.
Maths: 15-25 mixed questions a week and an error log. D&T: 8-12 technical terms per theory session; every NEA session must produce a tangible artefact/evidence item.

Time guide: school nights 60-100 minutes, Saturday 2.5-3 hours, Sunday 2-2.5 hours. Do not trade sleep for extra revision. If something clashes keep German retrieval (15-20 min), one English block and the week's priority topic: move, do not erase.
method: Mark every question with the official mark scheme, only after the attempt. For every lost mark write the missing fact or reasoning in an error log, then redo the question closed-book after 2-3 days and again after 7 days.
Log: date | board/spec point | paper series/year | component | question number | marks available | marks earned | lost-mark reason | retest date.
Use an older paper for practice and save a recent full paper for timed rehearsal. For a 6-marker use enough distinct, linked points; for evaluation include a justified conclusion.

weeks.title: Diagnose, establish retrieval routines, begin core content

blocks.subject: German

blocks.subject: Maths

blocks.subject: Physics

blocks.subject: German

blocks.subject: English Literature

blocks.subject: German
